_note: Daily info bite for the audio brief: one short, fun line read right after "Good morning, Waynesville! It's <day>." Picked by scripts/day-bite.mjs in this order: (1) holidays computed by rule (Thanksgiving, Easter, Mother's Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, clock changes, and the first day of each season at the exact equinox or solstice time, coded in day-bite.mjs); (2) a fixed-date entry below, by MM-DD; (3) a countdown (Christmas from the day after Thanksgiving, Thanksgiving in the week before); (4) on Mondays, today's sunrise, sunset and hours of daylight in Waynesville; (5) on other days, a line from "pool" below, rotating one per day so no line repeats until the pool has gone round. A pool entry is a sentence, or {"text": ..., "months": [1-12]} to use it only in those months. Pool lines must be true and evergreen, never date-specific; don't start them with "It's". A countdown is added after (1) or (2) when one is running. Each fixed entry is a sentence written for the ear; keep it under about 120 characters, light and true. Add entries freely; a date can hold a list, and the line is then picked by year so it changes year to year.

fixed.01-01: Happy New Year! It's also the birthday of General Anthony Wayne, our village's namesake, born on this day in 1745.
fixed.01-04: It's National Trivia Day, so here's one: Waynesville was laid out in 1797, before Ohio was even a state.
fixed.01-19: It's National Popcorn Day. Movie night, anyone?
fixed.01-21: It's Squirrel Appreciation Day, so give a nod to the busiest neighbors on your block.
fixed.01-23: It's National Pie Day. No judgment if that means pie for breakfast.
fixed.01-24: It's National Compliment Day. Go ahead and make someone's morning.
fixed.02-02: It's Groundhog Day. Whatever the groundhog says, spring officially arrives in about six and a half weeks.
fixed.02-09: It's National Pizza Day, a fine excuse to order from one of our local spots tonight.
fixed.02-11: Inventor Thomas Edison was born on this day in 1847, in Milan, Ohio.
fixed.02-14: Happy Valentine's Day! Downtown Waynesville makes for a pretty sweet date night.
fixed.02-20: On this day in 1962, Ohio's John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth.
fixed.02-27: It's International Polar Bear Day. Stay warm out there.
fixed.02-29: It's Leap Day, the bonus day that comes around only once every four years.
fixed.03-01: Happy birthday, Ohio! Our state joined the union on this day in 1803, the seventeenth state.
fixed.03-03: It's World Wildlife Day, a fine excuse to go look for some at Caesar Creek.
fixed.03-08: On this day in 1797, Samuel Heighway and his settlement party arrived at the spot that became Waynesville.
fixed.03-14: It's Pi Day. Celebrate with a slice of pie, three point one four of them if you're ambitious.
fixed.03-17: Happy St. Patrick's Day! Wear a little green today.
fixed.03-24: Warren County was created by an act of the Ohio General Assembly on this day in 1803.
fixed.04-01: It's April Fools' Day, so read everything twice today. Except this brief. This brief is real.
fixed.04-07: On this day in 1900, a fire swept Waynesville's Main Street and nearly wiped out the business block.
fixed.04-11: It's National Pet Day. Give the dog, the cat or the goldfish a little extra attention.
fixed.04-12: It's National Grilled Cheese Day. Lunch is decided.
fixed.04-22: It's Earth Day, a good day for a walk on the Little Miami Scenic Trail.
fixed.04-26: It's National Pretzel Day. Soft or crunchy, your call.
fixed.04-29: Kings Island first opened its gates to the public on this day in 1972.
fixed.05-04: It's Star Wars Day. May the Fourth be with you.
fixed.05-28: On this day in 1882, by a newspaper account, two boys fishing near Crosswick met a giant snake: the Crosswick Monster.
fixed.06-04: It's National Cheese Day. Say cheese.
fixed.06-14: It's Flag Day. Look for the stars and stripes along Main Street.
fixed.06-19: Today is Juneteenth, the federal holiday marking the end of slavery in the United States.
fixed.06-27: Poet Paul Laurence Dunbar was born on this day in 1872, in Dayton.
fixed.07-04: Happy Independence Day! Have a safe and happy Fourth.
fixed.07-17: It's World Emoji Day. Thumbs up.
fixed.07-20: On this day in 1969, Ohio's own Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the moon.
fixed.07-30: It's the International Day of Friendship. Call an old friend today.
fixed.08-03: The Treaty of Greenville was signed on this day in 1795, ceding most of present-day Ohio to the United States.
fixed.08-10: It's National S'mores Day. Fire pit, anyone?
fixed.08-19: It's National Aviation Day, set on the birthday of Dayton's Orville Wright, born in 1871.
fixed.08-20: On this day in 1794, General Anthony Wayne, our namesake, won the Battle of Fallen Timbers.
fixed.08-26: It's National Dog Day. Give your pup an extra treat today.
fixed.09-06: It's National Read a Book Day. The Mary L. Cook Public Library can help with that.
fixed.09-11: Today is Patriot Day, a day to remember the lives lost on September 11, 2001.
fixed.09-17: It's Constitution Day, marking the signing of the U.S. Constitution in 1787.
fixed.09-19: It's Talk Like a Pirate Day. Ahoy, Waynesville!
fixed.09-21: It's the International Day of Peace.
fixed.09-29: It's National Coffee Day. Treat yourself to a cup from a local shop.
fixed.10-03: The very first Ohio Sauerkraut Festival was held in Waynesville on this day in 1970.
fixed.10-04: It's National Taco Day. Plan accordingly.
fixed.10-29: It's National Cat Day. The cat already knew.
fixed.10-31: Happy Halloween! Drive slowly tonight and watch for trick-or-treaters.
fixed.11-03: It's National Sandwich Day. Build a good one.
fixed.11-11: Today is Veterans Day. Thank you to every veteran in our community for your service.
fixed.11-13: It's World Kindness Day. Hold a door, pay a compliment, check on a neighbor.
fixed.11-15: It's America Recycles Day. Rinse that jar.
fixed.11-21: It's World Hello Day. Say hello to someone new today.
fixed.12-04: It's National Cookie Day. You know what to do.
fixed.12-05: It's International Volunteer Day. Our Community page lists local groups that could use a hand.
fixed.12-07: Today is National Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day, honoring those lost on December 7, 1941.
fixed.12-15: General Anthony Wayne, our village's namesake, died on this day in 1796, a few months before Waynesville was laid out.
fixed.12-17: On this day in 1903, Dayton's Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight.
fixed.12-24: It's Christmas Eve. Wherever you're celebrating tonight, merry Christmas from all of us.
fixed.12-31: It's New Year's Eve. Have a safe and happy night, and see you next year.

pool: Waynesville is named for General "Mad" Anthony Wayne, the Revolutionary War hero.
Samuel Heighway, an engineer from Shropshire, England, laid out Waynesville in 1797.
Fun fact: Ohio's state fossil is the trilobite Isotelus, and fossil hunters find trilobites at Caesar Creek.
Quaker families began arriving in Waynesville in 1801. The Museum at the Friends Home tells their story.
Waynesville is often called the most haunted village in Ohio, a title popularized by Chris Woodyard's Haunted Ohio books.
The first Ohio Sauerkraut Festival, in 1970, drew about 1,500 people, who ate 528 pounds of sauerkraut.
Fun fact: Ohio's flag is the only U.S. state flag that isn't a rectangle.
The Sauerkraut Festival began as a merchants' sidewalk sale, with a sauerkraut dinner added to draw a crowd.
Waynesville calls itself the Antiques Capital of the Midwest, and Main Street makes the case.
Fun fact: Depending on who's counting, Waynesville has anywhere from 15 to more than 30 reportedly haunted sites.
Fun fact: Ohio's official state beverage is tomato juice.
Caesar Creek Lake, a few miles east of the village, covers about 2,830 acres.
Fossil hunters can search the Caesar Creek spillway with a free permit from the visitor center.
Fun fact: Seven U.S. presidents were born in Ohio.
The Hammel House Inn dates to 1822, and its ghost stories are a fixture of local ghost tours.
Got a question about something happening in town? Email the editor with Ask the Brief in the subject line.
Know of an event we're missing? Send it our way and we'll add it to the calendar.
Fun fact: The buckeye got its name because the nut looks like the eye of a deer.
Every event on our calendar has an add-to-calendar button. Find it at waynesville dot news slash events.
Ghost stories are part of the charm around here. If a door creaks downtown this morning, just say good morning.
Our Resources page puts local emergency numbers, crisis lines and county services in one place.
Fun fact: Ohio's name comes from an Iroquoian word meaning "great river."
Looking for a plumber, a groomer or a good lunch? Our business directory lists more than 200 local businesses.
If you're looking to get involved, our Community page lists local clubs, youth sports and volunteer groups.
The Ohio Sauerkraut Festival fills downtown Waynesville the second full weekend of every October.
Fun fact: Cincinnati's Red Stockings became baseball's first openly all-professional team in 1869.
Shop local when you can. Every dollar spent in town helps keep Main Street going.
Check on an older neighbor today. A quick hello goes a long way.
Fun fact: The Wright brothers built their first airplane in their Dayton bicycle shop.
By one count, the Sauerkraut Festival goes through about seven tons of sauerkraut in a single weekend.
Your library card at the Mary L. Cook Public Library opens up books, movies and more, all free.
Thanks for starting your day with us. If you like the Daily Brief, tell a friend.
Fun fact: Honey never spoils. Archaeologists have found edible honey in ancient Egyptian tombs.
Every source in today's brief is linked in the written edition at waynesville dot news.
Sauerkraut Festival crowds can top 300,000 people, many times the village's own population.
You can get the Daily Brief in your inbox each morning. Sign up at waynesville dot news.
Fun fact: An octopus has three hearts.
Grab your coffee. Here's what's happening around the village.
Whatever today brings, we hope it's a good one, Waynesville.
Fun fact: Sauerkraut is German for "sour cabbage," and it's just cabbage and salt, left to ferment.
Fun fact: A group of crows is called a murder.
A little kindness goes a long way. Hold a door for someone today.
Don't forget to drink some water today. Your future self will thank you.
Fun fact: Botanically speaking, bananas are berries and strawberries aren't.
One Sauerkraut Festival favorite is the German sundae: potatoes topped with cheese, bacon, sour cream, sauerkraut and an olive.
Spotted something new downtown? Let us know, and we might feature it.
News tip, event or correction? Reach us at editor at waynesville dot news.
Fun fact: Sea otters sometimes hold hands while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
If we ever get something wrong, tell us. We fix it and note the correction on the site.

If you pass a neighbor this morning, give a wave.

Drive safe today, and watch for walkers and cyclists on the back roads.

pool.text: Good day for a ride or a walk on the Little Miami Scenic Trail, which runs right through Corwin.
Heading to Caesar Creek? Bring sunscreen and plenty of water.
Sauerkraut Festival season is almost here. Downtown fills up the second full weekend of October.
School's out, so keep an eye out for kids on bikes around the neighborhoods.
Fall is a fine time to catch the colors along the Little Miami River.
Spring storms can pop up fast. Weather alerts on your phone are worth turning on.
With darker mornings, wear something bright if you're walking or running near the road.
Bundle up if you're heading out early, and give the windshield a few extra minutes.

pool: Warren County is named for Joseph Warren, a doctor and patriot killed at the Battle of Bunker Hill.
Charles Dickens stayed at the Golden Lamb in Lebanon in 1842.
The Little Miami was the first river in Ohio named a National Scenic River.
Fort Ancient, near Oregonia, is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks.
By tradition, Caesar Creek is named for a man called Caesar who lived among the Shawnee.
